newsitem.title: USA: Republican seen closing gap in Nebraska Senate race.
newsitem.headline: Republican seen closing gap in Nebraska Senate race.

text.p: Two new opinion polls have shaken up the Senate race in Nebraska, where Republicans now have their best shot at winning a Senate seat in this conservative state since 1972.

A poll released Thursday was the second in less than a week to show Omaha businessman Chuck Hagel closing to within five percentage points of Democratic Gov. Ben Nelson in the race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. James Exon.

A win in Nebraska, which even Republicans considered out of the question earlier in the campaign, would be a severe blow to Democratic hopes of winning a majority of the U.S. Senate, where they need three seats to gain control.
In the most recent poll, released Thursday by Omaha television station KMTV, 48 percent of the 800 people polled said they would vote for Nelson, while 43 percent would choose Hagel.

Several Republican candidates in House and Senate races nationwide have experienced sudden upswings in opinion polls this week, and some political analysts said the phenomenon may be linked to President Clinton's large lead over Bob Dole in the presidential campaign.

One theory suggests that U.S. voters, conscious of keeping a balance in government, may be turning to Republicans in national legislative races out of fear of giving Clinton a "blank check" in Washington.

"I think that argument might be especially attractive to Nebraskans, which might explain Hagel's surge in the polls," said John Comer, professor of political science at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.
Democrats responded to the theory with skepticism.
Comer noted that Nebraska tends to lean Republican. It was a major stronghold for George Bush in 1992, and registered Nebraska Republicans outnumber Democrats by 100,000.
